chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The pilgrims are of three types; the one with the best share is a man whose sins are forgiven, both what preceded and what followed, and Allah protects him from the punishment of the grave. And as for the one who follows him, it is a man whose sins are forgiven for what preceded, and he resumes deeds for what remains of his life. And as for the one who follows him, it is a man who is preserved regarding his family and his wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three levels of reward for Hajj pilgrims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates a hierarchical scale of Hajj rewards, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of pilgrimage as a means of expiation and divine protection. The highest tier promises comprehensive absolution and deliverance from the intermediate state of Barzakh (grave punishment), while lower tiers offer partial forgiveness or preservation of worldly ties, illustrating the nuanced relationship between ritual devotion and individual spiritual status.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said;

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The pilgrims are three, so the most superior of them in share is a man for whom his sins are Forgiven, whatever has preceded from it and whatever it delayed, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Saves him from the Punishment of the grave; and as for the one who follows him, so it is a man whose sins have been Forgiven for him, whatever has preceded from it, and he resumes the deeds in what is remaining from his life-span; and as for the one who follows him, so it is a man who is Protected regarding his family and his wealth’.
en.sarwar: 38. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm from abu al- Hassan al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

All of the people who stay in those hills, good or evil, Allah answers them all. People of good deed receive answers for the worldly and the hereafter and the people of evil deeds receive answer to their worldly matters.’”
